laws.rule: Angkor Archaeological Park passes are sold only by Angkor Enterprise: 1 day USD 37 (about A$52.56, RBA rate of 30 October 2026), 3 days USD 62 (use within 7 days), 7 days USD 72 (use within 30 days). Entry 5 am, closing 6.30 pm. 3-day and 7-day passes need a photo; passes bought elsewhere are not valid.
laws.heading: Angkor Enterprise, available tickets

laws.rule: Angkor Enterprise links the park's visitor code of conduct from its official site; staff check dress at temple entrances. The code requires shoulders and knees covered in the temples.

sources.title: Official Angkor Pass FAQ
sources.supports: sole seller, photo rule, code of conduct link (read directly 2026-11-05)

local-law.note: Dress rule from the APSARA code as summarised in search snapshots; read the code at the ticket office.

sites.name: Angkor Archaeological Park
sites.what: Capitals of the Khmer Empire, including Angkor Wat, Angkor Thom and Ta Prohm (UNESCO World Heritage).

access.opening: Entry from 5 am; closing 6.30 pm. A next-day 1-day ticket bought after 4.45 pm also lets you in that evening for sunset.
access.tickets: 1 day USD 37 (about AUD 53, RBA rate 30 October 2026); 3 days USD 62; 7 days USD 72. Angkor Enterprise is the only seller.

lore.text: Popular theories claim Angkor's temples were laid out to mirror the Draco constellation.
lore.label: popular lore, not an official source
